Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and helpful context on your production traffic. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Goal: understand end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets and whether Redwood hosted API can replace your current provider without regressions.
- FinLytics targets mentioned: target end-to-end p95 ~120ms, p99 ~300-400ms (TBD).
- Current provider baseline: you said some numbers on the call — could you confirm (see question below)?
- Key technical factors: streaming vs non-streaming, average/request token length, average/peak concurrency, peak throughput (rps), and whether you rely on prefix caching or reuse.

What we need from you to qualify and run a quick comparison test:
1) Confirm current provider observed metrics (p50/p95/p99) + any recent latency report you can share.
2) Typical payload sizes: average prompt tokens and average generated tokens.
3) Expected concurrency and peak throughput (requests per second or per minute).
4) Whether you require streaming responses (server-sent-chunk approach) for assistant UX.
5) Any SLA/cost constraints we should be aware of.

Attached is a short test plan and our SLO guidance to make the comparison apples-to-apples: finlytics_latency_test_plan.xlsx, redwood_slo_guidance.pdf. If you’re ok, we can run a 1-2 hour controlled load test from our hosted environment using your sample prompts (or ours if you prefer) and report end-to-end p50/p95/p99 with streaming and non-streaming runs. 

Proposed next step: if you can confirm the items above and share a time window (next 48-72 hours), we’ll schedule the test and loop in Priyom (SE) to design the load profile.

Thanks for the details and the report — useful data. Quick technical read:

Initial assessment:
- The numbers Samantha provided (p95 ~260ms / p99 ~520ms end-to-end) are consistent with a provider + edge + network stack. Our hosted API in us-east can typically hit p95 in the ~80-160ms range for small-context requests when using optimized models and streaming paths; p99 is more sensitive to bursty concurrency and network variance.

Key caveats and what we should measure (proposed controlled test):
1) End-to-end vs provider-only: we should measure both (a) raw provider processing time (server-side), and (b) full client-to-client end-to-end time to reflect your UX. The test plan Marissa sent covers both but please confirm you want both metrics.
2) Streaming: streaming adds overhead for chunking and network RTTs but improves perceived latency. We'll run streaming and non-streaming scenarios.
3) Sequence lengths: run at two profiles — short (prompt 40 tokens / gen 30 tokens) and long (prompt 200 tokens / gen 120 tokens) to capture token-size sensitivity.
4) Concurrency/throughput: run at baseline concurrency 25, ramp to 60, and a stress run at 100 to observe p99 tail behavior.
5) Affinity/caching: if you have repeated prefixes, let us know — caching can materially reduce p95.

Proposed test matrix (1-2 hours total):
- Scenario A (short, streaming): 25 concurrent, 15 min run
- Scenario B (short, non-streaming): 25 concurrent, 15 min run
- Scenario C (short, streaming): ramp 25→60 over 20 min
- Scenario D (long, streaming): 25 concurrent, 15 min run
- Scenario E (stress): 100 concurrent, 10 min run (observe p99 tail)

Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 for provider-only and end-to-end for each scenario, throughput, and CPU/GPU utilization snapshot from our side. If we see a meaningful regression at p99 we can recommend a Dedicated pool or config tweaks (batching, quantization profile, route to lower-latency model) as follow-up.

Requirements from FinLytics:
- Whitelisted client IPs (or an allowlist window) for the test harness if you run the client from your network, or credentials to run the client from our test runners using your sample prompts.
- Confirmation whether we should include their CDN/front-end in the loop for end-to-end measurements.

If that plan sounds good I can schedule the runs as soon as we have the IPs/permission and a 1-2 hour window. I’ll also prepare a short summary doc with expected baseline numbers and what to monitor.

—Priyom Das
